mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts by more than 10% over three months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances when HOUST declines by more than 10% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% in a month indicates a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 over three months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by less than 0.2%, it signals strong real demand growth without significant inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% MoM and CPIAUCSL increase < 0.2%
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% MoM and CPIAUCSL increases by less than 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate falls below 2% year-over-year, it indicates a monetary policy that is too tight for the current economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is above 2% and GDPC1 YoY growth is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in a month, coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 150,000, signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month and PAYEMS increase > 150,000
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% in a month and PAYEMS increases by more than 150,000.
